//: lint_silent_row_drop baseline — an invlang row leaving a loop by continue/break/bare return with neither a ParseWarning nor a landing unconditionally on that path (#876). Roles are derived structurally, never from a name list: the PROJECTOR is a class that both holds list[ParseWarning] state and raises one, the TOKENIZER is a function whose return annotation mentions Block (resolved by origin, not spelling). Only the EXPLICIT escape is mechanized — the implicit drop (a dispatch arm returning 'handled' without projecting, an if/elif chain with no else, a suppressed conversion) is out of scope, so a clean run is NOT proof the parser drops nothing. Fingerprint is file:function:escape-kind:guard (no line number). CI fails on a site absent here or on an un-triaged entry. Regenerate: python scripts/lint/lint_silent_row_drop.py --update-baseline. Every entry needs a reason; "" is refused.

entries.defender/skills/invlang/parser.py:_Proje: TRUE POSITIVE, filed as #876 — a `:S shelved` row whose hyp_id cell is empty is dropped with no ParseWarning, so a shelved hypothesis silently never reaches any lead's `shelved` list. This is the gate's sharpest evidence: three lines below it, the missing-by_lead row on the SAME loop DOES warn ('shelved row has no lead attribution') and is duly cleared by this gate. Baselined, not fixed — landing the gate must not change parser.py.

TRUE POSITIVE, filed as #876 — the `is_conclude_empty_marker(hid)` half is the documented `none`/`n/a` empty-array marker and is legitimately not a row, but the `not hid` half is a real drop: a `:T surviving_hypotheses` row with an empty hyp_id vanishes from `conclude.surviving_hypotheses` with nothing raised, and the close then reasons over a shortened survivor set. One guard, two cases; splitting them is the fix and belongs to #876, not to this gate's landing.

FALSE POSITIVE — documented same-site re-emission. `_register_hypotheses`'s own docstring states the contract: re-declaring an id at the SAME site is a re-emission and the first declaration stands SILENTLY, because that is exactly what `_extend_by_id` does to the list and what `_walkers.all_hypotheses` does on the read side. Warning here would fire on the sanctioned append-only shape. Only the cross-site case is unrecoverable, and that one already calls `self._warn(...)` on the very next line — which the gate clears.

TRUE POSITIVE, filed as #876 — a hypothesis row whose `id` cell is absent or not a string is skipped before it can enter `hypotheses_by_id`/`prologue_hypothesis_ids`, with no ParseWarning. Every later `:H h-NNN.preds` / `.authz` sub-block that names it then resolves to nothing, which is the same class of unfulfilled contract #876 was opened for. Baselined, not fixed — this gate owns no parser.py change.

FALSE POSITIVE — the loop inside the drop-reporter itself. `_warn_repeated_ids` exists to compare ids within one block; a row with no readable id cannot be checked for a REPEATED id, so skipping it drops nothing (the row is still projected by the caller, which is the loop that owns it). The house cure for a single-site false alarm like this is the inline `# lint-row-drop: ok — <reason>` marker on the `continue` itself; it is baselined here instead only because landing this gate is forbidden from editing defender/skills/invlang/parser.py. Move it to the inline marker on the next parser.py change and drop this entry.
entries.defender/skills/invlang/parser.py:_token: FALSE POSITIVE — a state transition, not a row. The `### story` header sets `in_story = True` and clears `cur`; the line consumed is the heading itself, so there is no row to land or to warn about. The rows the heading affects are handled by the `in_story or cur is None` escape below, which this gate does flag.

TRUE POSITIVE, filed as #876 — the tokenizer half, and this gate's motivating finding. A non-blank, non-header line arriving while `in_story` is set, or before any block header has opened `cur`, is discarded inside `_tokenize_fence` with no ParseWarning: the line never becomes a Block row, so no projector and no validator can ever see that it existed. Every downstream count is computed over a document the tokenizer silently shortened.

FALSE POSITIVE — a blank line. `stripped` is empty, so there is no row in hand: nothing was dropped and there is nothing a ParseWarning could name. Whitespace between fenced blocks is part of the format, not a malformed row.
